abstract: We present the case of a 14-year-old girl in whom a myelodysplastic syndrome was diagnosed 9 months after surgical resection and chemotherapy for an ovarian germ cell tumor. Cells from her marrow were characterized by trisomy 8 and an isochromosome 12p, a marker that appears to be unique to germ cell tumors. The presence of the same two anomalies in her original tumor was demonstrated by fluorescence in situ hybridization study of interphase cells in paraffin-embedded tissues and thus provided strong evidence that the two neoplasms had a common clonal origin.
abstract_ja: 14歳の女児において、卵巣胚細胞腫瘍に対する外科的切除および化学療法の9か月後に骨髄異形成症候群が診断された。骨髄由来の細胞は、トリソミー8と12p等染色体(isochromosome 12p)を特徴とし、これは胚細胞腫瘍に特有と考えられるマーカーである。同じ2つの異常が、原発腫瘍においてもパラフィン包埋組織の間期細胞に対する蛍光in situハイブリダイゼーション検査で確認され、2つの腫瘍が共通のクローン起源を持つことを強く示した。
